blindSummary: This state/province has two documented departures from the national position. Its legislature is among the six that have enacted no legal gender-recognition procedure at all (an international human-rights organisation, March 2025), keeping trans people's documents permanently mismatched - the single most visitor-relevant legal fact in the country, since a mismatched document is what prompts a police check. And the country dossier names this border state/province among the units where armed-group control amplifies trans-specific risk: armed groups and local police, not the penal code, decide how a gender-nonconforming person is treated, and both have documented patterns of extortion and sexual exploitation of trans women in detention.
